learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basic concepts about Descriptive Statistics, Probability, and fundamental probabilistic models.
Introduce students to the basic methods of Statistical Inference: Parameter Estimation (point and Confidence Intervals) and Hypothesis Testing.
Assess the need for IT tools and ICTs and learn to use the appropriate tool to apply the suitable statistical procedures more quickly and accurately in each case.

syllabus_topics: What is statistics? Fundamental objectives of statistics.
Computer applications in statistics.
Introduction to Excel spreadsheet, statistical packages and data analysis.
General concepts: Statistical Population, Statistical Unit or individual, Sample. Statistical Variables.
Statistical description of a variable: Frequency distributions, absolute, relative, cumulative frequency. Frequency table. Grouping. Choice of intervals.
Graphical representations of statistical variables.
Characteristic measures of a statistical variable: Measures of centralization, Measures of dispersion, Measures of asymmetry and kurtosis, Moments.
Descriptive statistics. Description of one-dimensional random variables.
Two-dimensional statistical variables. Introduction.
Joint frequency distribution: marginal distributions, conditional distributions.
Graphical representations. Scatter plot.
Regression. Linear dependence.
Measures of linear dependence. Correlation.
Descriptive statistics. Description of two-dimensional random variables. Regression and correlation.
Random experiments. Sample space and events. Operations with events. Boolean algebra of random events.
Definition of probability, frequentist and axiomatic definition. Probability in finite sample spaces: Laplace's rule.
Combinatorial analysis.
Conditional probability and independence of events: Conditional probability, Multiplication rule, Independence of events, Total probability theorem, Bayes' theorem. Applications.
Concept of random variables (R.V.), discrete R.V. and continuous R.V.
Discrete random variables. Probability function and distribution function.
Continuous random variables. Probability density function and distribution function.
Characteristics associated with an R.V.: Expectation, Variance and Standard Deviation. Moments.
General probability results: Markov's and Chebyshev's inequality.
Two-dimensional random variables. Marginal, conditional distributions. Characteristics of two-dimensional R.V. Covariance. Correlation coefficient. Independence of R.V.

Models of discrete distributions: Bernoulli experiments, Bernoulli distribution, Binomial distribution, Geometric distribution, Negative binomial distribution, Poisson distribution, Discrete uniform distribution.

Models of continuous distributions: Uniform distribution, Exponential distribution, NORMAL distribution. Standardized Normal variable. Distributions associated with the Normal: Pearson's Χ², Student's T, Fisher-Snedecor's F. Other distributions: Gamma, Beta distributions.
Models of probability distributions.
Fundamental concepts: Population and sampling. Simple random sampling.
Estimation. Concept of statistic. Some important statistics: sample mean, sample variance and standard deviation.
Point estimation. Some important estimators. Properties of a good estimator.
Interval estimation with confidence intervals. Sampling distribution of the most important estimators: proportion, mean, variance, difference of means, ...
Most important confidence intervals (CI): CI for the mean, for the proportion, for the variance, for the difference of means, for the difference of proportions, for the equality of variances.
Determination of sample size.
Inference. Confidence intervals.
Introduction. Fundamental concepts for hypothesis tests: Hypothesis, test statistic, critical region, significance and confidence level, errors in a test, power of the test.
The concept of p-value.

Examples of the most common parametric hypothesis tests (HT): HT for the mean, HT for the variance, HT for the proportion, HT for the equality of means, HT for the equality of variances, HT for the equality of proportions of means etc.
Introduction to non-parametric tests.
Inference. Hypothesis tests.
Optimization, Linear Programming, simplex algorithm.
Introduction to Design of Experiments (ANOVA). Introduction to Statistical Quality Control.
Extension of statistics.

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or partial exams (including computer component)
Exploitation of practical activities (computer labs, visits, etc.)
Resolution and delivery of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: The course is passed if the student obtains a final grade equal to or greater than 5 points in any call (ordinary or extraordinary), regardless of the chosen evaluation system (global or continuous). Continuous evaluation activities performed during the semester (semester written theoretical-practical tests, activities resolution and delivery) are not recoverable.
